coalescence_plan: A + B -> ONE CPU deployment decision (2nd-order set). A (rotation-only reachable) says whether rotation alone suffices on ggml-cpu; B (codec ports) says whether the full PolarQuant codec is needed. Single measured criterion: 'KLD within +1% of q8_0 at >=0.85x decode on the 4-core ARM box.' Outcomes: rotation-only-deployable | codec-port-needed | CPU-turbo-dead. No MVP until this set has one number.

B + C -> ONE codec, two backends (2nd-order set). If the same block-32 format + the pinned 4-bit centroid table (outer 0.24021) yields identical KLD on ggml-cpu and on sm_75 CUDA, the town gets a single source of truth for KV quantization. Test the B2 conformance test on BOTH backends.

A + C -> rotation-first-order across both iron. Run the identical rotation-only q4_0 KLD comparison on CPU (rank 4) and on the 2070S (rank 9). If both show the same recovery of the turbo4 margin, rotation is substrate-independent and the port budget goes to the codec, not the rotation.

D + E -> ONE oracle for representation vs quantization (2nd-order set). Rank 2's routing-TV/KLD currency is the common scale that makes the byte-neuron (rank 11), oscillator rotation (rank 11) and GQA group-death (rank 12) comparable at equal bits. Without the oracle, every E comparison is unfalsifiable.

Rank 1 gates all E spending. No Kuramoto/oscillator/byte-neuron experiment runs before the ~5-minute sweep of the dead-head artifact. The prior critic already computed lift ~1.0001 and Spearman +0.268; reproducing it is the entry ticket, not an experiment.

Every later lever (KV quant, ternary, looping, per-head KV, behavior projection) is evaluated as a bytes-touched delta before it runs. Rank 5 supplies the ISA constant.

One Camber burst, not four: the cross-arch attribution A/B (rank 9 / bonsai B5) is the same A/B and answers both the PTQ1_0 kernel-gain question and the TurboQuant decode-tax question. Second-order set: 'Turing kernel gap is arch | kernel ceiling.'
